claim: HIV-1 entry into cells requires binding of the viral envelope glycoprotein (Env) to receptor CD4 and coreceptor.
source: HIV-1 entry into cells requires binding of the viral envelope glycoprotein (Env) to receptor CD4 and coreceptor.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in HIV biology, supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: Imaging of individual Env molecules on native virions shows Env trimers to be dynamic, spontaneously transitioning between three distinct well-populated conformational states.
source: Imaging of individual Env molecules on native virions shows Env trimers to be dynamic, spontaneously transitioning between three distinct well-populated conformational states: a pre-triggered Env (State 1), a default intermediate (State 2) and a three-CD4-bound conformation (State 3), which can be stabilized by binding of CD4 and coreceptor-surrogate antibody 17b.
evidence: This claim is supported by smFRET imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The default intermediate configuration is asymmetric, with individual protomers adopting distinct conformations.
source: Here, using single-molecule Fluorescence Resonance Energy Transfer (smFRET), we show the default intermediate configuration to be asymmetric, with individual protomers adopting distinct conformations.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by mixed trimer experiments.

claim: During entry, the asymmetric intermediate forms when a single CD4 molecule engages the trimer.
source: During entry, this asymmetric intermediate forms when a single CD4 molecule engages the trimer.
evidence: This is supported by mixed trimer experiments showing State 2 stabilization with single CD4 binding.

claim: The trimer can transition to State 3 by binding additional CD4 molecules and coreceptor.
source: The trimer can then transition to State 3 by binding additional CD4 molecules and coreceptor.
evidence: This is supported by experiments with dodecameric CD4 and 17b antibody.

claim: Env is a trimer with each protomer consisting of two subunits: the surface subunit gp120 that binds to receptor and coreceptor, and the transmembrane subunit gp41 that mediates fusion of viral and cellular membranes.
source: Env is a trimer with each protomer consisting of two subunits: the surface subunit gp120 that binds to receptor and coreceptor, and the transmembrane subunit gp41 that mediates fusion of viral and cellular membranes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HIV-1 Env structure.

claim: CD4 binding induces conformational changes in Env that expose structural elements required for coreceptor binding including the V3 loop and the bridging sheet.
source: CD4 binding induces conformational changes in Env that expose structural elements required for coreceptor binding including the V3 loop and the bridging sheet (Trkola et al., 1996; Kwong et al., 1998; Huang et al., 2007; Liu et al., 2008; Pancera et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2016; Herschhorn et al., 2017; Ozorowski et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous structural studies.

claim: Binding of coreceptor triggers additional conformational changes in gp41, including the formation of an extended gp41 structure that subsequently collapses into a stable six-helix bundle.
source: Binding of coreceptor triggers additional conformational changes in gp41, including the formation of an extended gp41 structure that subsequently collapses into a stable six-helix bundle, which is thought to drive viral and cellular membranes together for fusion (Pancera et al., 2010; Blumenthal et al., 2012; Harrison, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous structural and mechanistic studies.

claim: Env's capacity to undergo extensive conformational changes is critical for virus entry.
source: Correspondingly, Env's capacity to undergo extensive conformational changes is critical for virus entry.
evidence: This is inferred from the described conformational changes required for entry.

claim: Env evades immune surveillance through 'conformational masking'.
source: At the same time, Env evades immune surveillance through 'conformational masking' (Kwong et al., 2002), which protects key functional elements within the trimer from being recognized by antibodies.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work on conformational masking.

claim: Conformational masking renders most Env-targeting antibodies non-neutralizing.
source: This feature renders most Env-targeting antibodies non-neutralizing.
evidence: This is inferred from the conformational masking mechanism.

claim: A portion of patients develop potent broadly neutralizing antibodies that can prevent immunodeficiency virus infections in animal models.
source: However, a portion of patients develop potent broadly neutralizing antibodies that can prevent immunodeficiency virus infections in animal models, lower the viral load when administered to HIV-1-infected patients and can restore immunological control in the absence of antiretroviral therapy (ART) in non-human primates (Wu et al., 2010; Walker et al., 2011; Klein et al., 2012; Caskey et al., 2015; Gautam et al., 2016; Lu et al., 2016; Schoofs et al., 2016; Nishimura et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to clinical and animal studies.

claim: Antibodies that are broadly neutralizing tend to recognize closed Env conformations.
source: Antibodies that are broadly neutralizing tend to recognize closed Env conformations (Munro et al., 2014; Guttman et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: smFRET analysis revealed that single Env protomers spontaneously transit between three distinct conformational states exhibiting low-, intermediate- and high-FRET values.
source: smFRET analysis revealed that single Env protomers spontaneously transit between three distinct conformational states exhibiting low-, intermediate- and high-FRET values (Munro et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous smFRET work.

claim: The unliganded Env prefers a low-FRET pre-triggered conformation.
source: The unliganded Env prefers a low-FRET pre-triggered conformation.
evidence: This is supported by FRET histogram data showing predominant low-FRET state.

claim: In the presence of soluble CD4 (D1D2 domain, sCD4), and the additional presence of the coreceptor-surrogate antibody 17b, some Env trimers could be stabilized in high-FRET and intermediate-FRET conformations, respectively.
source: In the presence of soluble CD4 (D1D2 domain, sCD4), and the additional presence of the coreceptor-surrogate antibody 17b, some Env trimers could be stabilized in high-FRET and intermediate-FRET conformations, respectively (Munro et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous smFRET experiments.

claim: The low-FRET state corresponds to the pre-triggered conformation.
source: Various lines of evidence suggest that the low-FRET state corresponds to the pre-triggered conformation: (1) it is the most populated conformation of the unliganded Env; (2) it is more populated in a clinical isolate such as HIV-1JR-FL that is more neutralization-resistant than the laboratory-adapted HIV-1NL4-3; and (3) it is stabilized by broadly neutralizing antibodies, and the small-molecule conformational blocker BMS-626529 (Munro et al., 2014; Pancera et al., 2014; Kwon et al., 2015; Herschhorn et al., 2017; Pancera et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple lines of evidence including population analysis and antibody binding.

claim: Dodecameric CD4 (sCD4D1D2-Igαtp) is a potent neutralizer of HIV-1.
source: Here we provide smFRET analysis that clarify the nature of the intermediate-FRET and high-FRET Env conformations. Through smFRET measurements, we demonstrated that dodecameric CD4 (sCD4D1D2-Igαtp), which is a potent neutralizer of HIV-1, stabilizes the intermediate-FRET State 3 of the Env in three strains HIV-1NL4-3, HIV-1JR-FL and HIV-1BG505.
evidence: This is supported by neutralization assays and smFRET data in the manuscript.

claim: Dodecameric CD4 (sCD4D1D2-Igαtp) stabilizes the intermediate-FRET State 3 of the Env in three strains HIV-1NL4-3, HIV-1JR-FL and HIV-1BG505.
source: Through smFRET measurements, we demonstrated that dodecameric CD4 (sCD4D1D2-Igαtp), which is a potent neutralizer of HIV-1, stabilizes the intermediate-FRET State 3 of the Env in three strains HIV-1NL4-3, HIV-1JR-FL and HIV-1BG505.
evidence: This is directly supported by FRET histogram data in Figure 1.

claim: No difference was observed in predominant conformational state of Env bound to CD4/17b, to JRC-II-191 (a CD4 small molecule mimetic), or to sCD4D1D2-Igαtp, all of which corresponded to the open three-CD4-bound conformation of the trimer (State 3).
source: We observed no difference in predominant conformational state of Env bound to CD4/17b, to JRC-II-191 (a CD4 small molecule mimetic), or to sCD4D1D2-Igαtp, all of which corresponded to the open three-CD4-bound conformation of the trimer (State 3).
evidence: This is supported by FRET data comparing different ligands.

claim: By using a mixed trimer assay, the intermediate configuration of State two was identified to be an asymmetric Env trimer.
source: Moreover, by using a mixed trimer assay, we identified the intermediate configuration of State two to be an asymmetric Env trimer.
evidence: This is supported by mixed trimer experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: In the asymmetric trimer configuration, a single CD4 can engage the trimer such that individual protomers adopt distinct conformations.
source: In this configuration, a single CD4 can engage the trimer such that individual protomers adopt distinct conformations.
evidence: This is supported by mixed trimer experiments showing different FRET states for different protomers.

claim: An asymmetric trimer is a prevalent functional intermediate, which can open further either spontaneously or through binding to additional CD4 molecules or to coreceptor.
source: An asymmetric trimer is thus a prevalent functional intermediate, which can open further either spontaneously or through binding to additional CD4 molecules or to coreceptor.
evidence: This is supported by experiments showing State 3 stabilization with multiple CD4 or coreceptor binding.

claim: The insertion of Q3 and A1 tags into the variable loops V1 and V4 of gp120 for enzymatic labeling was validated by infectivity assays, protein expression and antibody neutralizations.
source: The insertion of Q3 and A1 tags into the variable loops V1 and V4 of gp120 for enzymatic labeling was validated by infectivity assays, protein expression and antibody neutralizations, indicating that the Env functions remained minimally affected even in the 100% dually tagged virus (Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: Env functions remained minimally affected even in the 100% dually tagged virus.
source: The insertion of Q3 and A1 tags into the variable loops V1 and V4 of gp120 for enzymatic labeling was validated by infectivity assays, protein expression and antibody neutralizations, indicating that the Env functions remained minimally affected even in the 100% dually tagged virus (Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is supported by infectivity and neutralization data in supplementary figures.

claim: FRET trajectories and histograms showed that the gp120 protomers in unliganded HIV-1 Env predominantly resided in a low-FRET conformation, but had inherent access to both intermediate- and high-FRET conformations.
source: In agreement with previous results (Munro et al., 2014), FRET trajectories and histograms showed that the gp120 protomers in unliganded HIV-1 Env predominantly resided in a low-FRET conformation, but had inherent access to both intermediate- and high-FRET conformations (Figure 1A and B, left).
evidence: This is directly shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: The HIV-1 isolates JR-FL and BG505 exhibited a higher occupancy of the pre-triggered low-FRET state as compared to the lab-adapted NL4-3.
source: Consistent with the features of Tier two viruses, the HIV-1 isolates JR-FL and BG505 (Koyanagi et al., 1987; Wu et al., 2006) exhibited a higher occupancy of the pre-triggered low-FRET state as compared to the lab-adapted NL4-3 (compare Figures 1E and H, B).
evidence: This is shown by comparing FRET histograms in Figure 1.

claim: The unliganded HIV-1NL4-3 Env frequently transitioned between the low-FRET and high-FRET states, and between the high- and intermediate-FRET states.
source: The unliganded HIV-1NL4-3 Env frequently transitioned between the low-FRET and high-FRET states, and between the high- and intermediate-FRET states; whereas transitions between low- and intermediate-FRET were rarely observed.
evidence: This is shown in the transition density plot in Figure 1B.

claim: Transitions between low- and intermediate-FRET were rarely observed.
source: The unliganded HIV-1NL4-3 Env frequently transitioned between the low-FRET and high-FRET states, and between the high- and intermediate-FRET states; whereas transitions between low- and intermediate-FRET were rarely observed.
evidence: This is shown in the transition density plot in Figure 1B.

claim: The high-FRET state represents a default conformational intermediate during opening of the Env trimer.
source: Given that the low-FRET state corresponds to a mature pre-triggered conformation of the trimer, these data suggest that the high-FRET state represents a default conformational intermediate during opening of the Env trimer.
evidence: This is inferred from the transition pattern observed in TDP.

claim: Addition of sCD4 (0.1 mg/ml) stabilized HIV-1NL4-3 Env in State 2.
source: Consistent with previous observations, addition of sCD4 (0.1 mg/ml) stabilized HIV-1NL4-3 Env in State 2 (Figure 1C, left).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C FRET histogram.

claim: sCD4D1D2-Igαtp is 300 to 1000-fold more potent in neutralizing HIV-1 than sCD4.
source: To clarify the response of HIV-1NL4-3 Env to receptor CD4, a dodecameric CD4 oligomer (sCD4D1D2-Igαtp, 0.1 mg/ml), which is 300 to 1000-fold more potent in neutralizing HIV-1 than sCD4, was used to provide a high local CD4 density (Arthos et al., 2002; Kwong et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies on dodecameric CD4.

claim: sCD4D1D2-Igαtp stabilized HIV-1NL4-3 Env in State 3.
source: Strikingly, sCD4D1D2-Igαtp stabilized HIV-1NL4-3 Env in State 3 (Figure 1D), indicating that both sCD4/17b (Munro et al., 2014) and an oligomerized CD4, both stabilize HIV-1NL4-3 Env in the three-CD4-bound trimer configuration (State 3).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1D FRET histogram.

claim: Both sCD4/17b and an oligomerized CD4 stabilize HIV-1NL4-3 Env in the three-CD4-bound trimer configuration (State 3).
source: Strikingly, sCD4D1D2-Igαtp stabilized HIV-1NL4-3 Env in State 3 (Figure 1D), indicating that both sCD4/17b (Munro et al., 2014) and an oligomerized CD4, both stabilize HIV-1NL4-3 Env in the three-CD4-bound trimer configuration (State 3).
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the effects of different ligands on FRET states.

claim: Both HIV-1JR-FL and HIV-1BG505 were less responsive to sCD4, with only small increases in the occupancies of States 2 and 3.
source: In contrast to the NL4-3 isolate, both HIV-1JR-FL and HIV-1BG505 were less responsive to sCD4, with only small increases in the occupancies of States 2 and 3 (Figure 1F and I) although sCD4 and 17b stabilized both in State 3 (Munro et al., 2014) (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1F and I FRET histograms.

claim: Addition of the dodecameric sCD4D1D2-Igαtp stabilized both HIV-1JR-FL and HIV-1BG505 in State 3.
source: Importantly, as was observed for HIV-1NL4-3 Env, addition of the dodecameric sCD4D1D2-Igαtp stabilized both HIV-1JR-FL and HIV-1BG505 in State 3 (Figure 1G and J).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1G and J FRET histograms.

claim: For all three HIV-1 isolates the intermediate-FRET State 3 corresponds to the three-CD4-bound conformation.
source: This suggests that for all three HIV-1 isolates the intermediate-FRET State 3 corresponds to the three-CD4-bound conformation (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is inferred from the consistent stabilization of State 3 by dodecameric CD4 across all three strains.

claim: The D368R mutation in the CD4-binding pocket of Env reduces affinity for CD4.
source: To distinguish between these possibilities, we took advantage of the D368R mutation in the CD4-binding pocket of Env that reduces affinity for CD4 (Olshevsky et al., 1990).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work on the D368R mutation.

claim: The D368R mutant of HIV-1NL4-3 Env was resistant to the neutralization of both sCD4 and sCD4D1D2-Igαtp.
source: The D368R mutant of HIV-1NL4-3 Env was resistant to the neutralization of both sCD4 and sCD4D1D2-Igαtp (Figure 2A, Table 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2A neutralization curves and Table 2.

claim: Trimers that uniformly contained the D368R mutation exhibited similar conformational landscapes to that of wild-type HIV-1, and did not respond to sCD4 and sCD4D1D2-Igαtp as WT HIV-1NL4-3.
source: Trimers that uniformly contained the D368R mutation exhibited similar conformational landscapes to that of wild-type HIV-1, and did not respond to sCD4 and sCD4D1D2-Igαtp as WT HIV-1NL4-3 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A FRET histograms.

claim: The single D368R mutation exhibited little or no conformational effects on the trimer.
source: Thus, unlike the double mutant D368R/E370R that was stabilized in State 1 (Munro et al., 2014) (likely due to E370R interfering with the adoption of the bridging sheet), the single D368R mutation exhibited little or no conformational effects on the trimer.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing FRET histograms of D368R mutant with wild-type.

claim: smFRET analysis for the mixed HIV-1NL4-3 trimer 1 revealed a clear State 3 stabilization by sCD4.
source: smFRET analysis for the mixed HIV-1NL4-3 trimer 1 revealed a clear State 3 stabilization by sCD4 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2D FRET histogram.

claim: gp120 bound to CD4 adopts a State 3 conformation regardless of the CD4 occupancy elsewhere within the trimer, even when only a single CD4 molecule engages the trimer.
source: Thus, gp120 bound to CD4 adopts a State 3 conformation regardless of the CD4 occupancy elsewhere within the trimer, even when only a single CD4 molecule engages the trimer.
evidence: This is inferred from the mixed trimer 1 experiment showing State 3 in the CD4-bound protomer.

claim: Imaging of the HIV-1NL4-3 mixed trimer two restored the high occupancy of the State two conformation.
source: Strikingly, despite the heterogeneity in the population of trimers, imaging of the HIV-1NL4-3 mixed trimer two restored the high occupancy of the State two conformation (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2E FRET histogram.

claim: The observed high-FRET state likely originates from an unbound gp120 protomer adjacent to a CD4-bound protomer.
source: Hence, the observed high-FRET state likely originates from an unbound gp120 protomer adjacent to a CD4-bound protomer.
evidence: This is inferred from the mixed trimer 2 experiment showing State 2 in protomers adjacent to CD4-bound protomer.

claim: Since the State three and State two stabilizations were observed for the same single-CD4 condition, but with dyes placed either into the protomer that binds a single CD4 or adjacent to it, this trimer must be asymmetric with protomers adopting distinct conformations.
source: Since the State three and State two stabilizations were observed for the same single-CD4 condition, but with dyes placed either into the protomer that binds a single CD4 or adjacent to it, this trimer must be asymmetric with protomers adopting distinct conformations (Figure 2L).
evidence: This is inferred from comparing mixed trimer 1 and 2 results.

claim: The engineering of mixed trimers that can only bind a single CD4 allowed the asymmetric trimer to be stabilized, confirming that the high-FRET of the default structural intermediate originates from protomers adjacent to a single bound CD4 molecule.
source: Intriguingly, the engineering of mixed trimers that can only bind a single CD4 allowed the asymmetric trimer to be stabilized, confirming that the high-FRET of the default structural intermediate originates from protomers adjacent to a single bound CD4 molecule (Figure 2G,H,J,K).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2G,H,J,K for JR-FL and BG505 mixed trimers.

claim: The broad high-FRET peaks in sCD4D1D2-Igαtp-bound mixed trimer two suggest a potential continuum of various conformational states.
source: The broad high-FRET peaks in sCD4D1D2-Igαtp-bound mixed trimer two suggest a potential continuum of various conformational states.
evidence: This is inferred from the shape of the FRET histogram peaks.

claim: The trimer spontaneously opens and closes through an asymmetric trimer configuration.
source: These data support the hypothesis that the trimer spontaneously opens and closes through an asymmetric trimer configuration.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of State 2 in unliganded Env and its stabilization by single CD4.

claim: During virus entry, a single CD4 may initially engage a closed trimer.
source: Moreover, during virus entry, a single CD4 may initially engage a closed trimer (Kwon et al., 2015; Hu et al., 2017), and a very early version of this intermediate may be presented in the single CD4-bound structure of the Env trimer stabilized by the DS-SOSIP (Liu et al., 2017) when not fixed by DS mutation, CD4 binding to the trimer would induce the CD4-bound conformation in the bound protomer (Figure 2L).
evidence: This is supported by citations and inferred from the asymmetric trimer data.

claim: Binding of a single CD4 may loosen interaction of the V1/V2 loops in the trimer association domain so that neighboring protomers can adopt a conformation in which the V1 and V4 loops are closer to each other.
source: Binding of a single CD4 may loosen interaction of the V1/V2 loops in the trimer association domain so that neighboring protomers can adopt a conformation in which the V1 and V4 loops are closer to each other.
evidence: This is a mechanistic speculation based on the observed high-FRET in adjacent protomers.

claim: When two CD4 molecules are bound to the Env trimer, the ligand-free protomer adopted the State three conformation, indicating that the trimer had fully opened.
source: Interestingly, when two CD4 molecules are bound to the Env trimer, the ligand-free protomer adopted the State three conformation, indicating that the trimer had fully opened (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B-D for mixed trimer 3.

claim: Binding of two CD4 molecules is enough to flip the third protomer open indicating cooperativity between the three protomers.
source: Binding of two CD4 molecules is enough to flip the third protomer open indicating cooperativity between the three protomers.
evidence: This is inferred from the mixed trimer 3 data showing State 3 in the unbound protomer.

claim: The data are consistent with previous reports on the necessity of binding of multiple CD4 molecules to Env, as well as CD4 clustering.
source: Our data are consistent with previous reports on the necessity of binding of multiple CD4 molecules to Env, as well as CD4 clustering (Yang et al., 2006; Salzwedel and Berger, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The mixed trimer two bound by both a single sCD4 molecule and 17b also adopted the State three conformation.
source: We observed that the mixed trimer two bound by both a single sCD4 molecule and 17b also adopted the State three conformation (Figure 3F–H).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3F-H FRET histograms.

claim: Coreceptor binding would be sufficient to trigger the complete opening of the single-CD4 bound asymmetric trimer.
source: This suggests that coreceptor binding would also be sufficient to trigger the complete opening of the single-CD4 bound asymmetric trimer (Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the 17b binding data on mixed trimer 2.

claim: Before binding of sCD4, the relative free energy of HIV-1NL4-3 State 2 was 0.37 kBT higher than State 1.
source: Before binding of sCD4, the relative free energy of HIV-1NL4-3 State 2 was 0.37 kBT higher than State 1 (Figure 4A, left).
evidence: This is calculated from FRET histogram occupancies shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Following binding of sCD4, the free energy of State 2 was 0.54 kBT lower than State 1, resulting in a net change of −0.91 kBT.
source: Following binding of sCD4, the free energy of State 2 was 0.54 kBT lower than State 1, resulting in a net change of −0.91 kBT.
evidence: This is calculated from FRET histogram occupancies.

claim: sCD4 binding decreased the activation energy for the transitions from State one and State three into State 2, and increased the activation energy for transitions out of State 2.
source: With respect to activation energies, sCD4 binding decreased the activation energy for the transitions from State one and State three into State 2, and increased the activation energy for transitions out of State 2.
evidence: This is calculated from transition rate constants shown in Table 1.

claim: The predominant effect of sCD4D1D2-Igαtp binding was to stabilize State 3.
source: In contrast, the predominant effect of sCD4D1D2-Igαtp binding was to stabilize State 3 (Figure 4A, right, Figure 1D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A and Figure 1D.

claim: Before sCD4D1D2-Igαtp binding, the free energy of State 3 was 0.11 kBT lower than State 2.
source: Before sCD4D1D2-Igαtp binding, the free energy of State 3 was 0.11 kBT lower than State 2.
evidence: This is calculated from FRET histogram occupancies.

claim: Following sCD4D1D2-Igαtp binding the free energy of State 3 was 0.69 kBT lower than the liganded State 2.
source: Following sCD4D1D2-Igαtp binding the free energy of State 3 was 0.69 kBT lower than the liganded State 2.
evidence: This is calculated from FRET histogram occupancies.

claim: The unliganded HIV-1JR-FL and HIV-1BG505 Envs more stably adopted State one as compared to the HIV-1NL4-3 Env.
source: We then repeated these experiments for the clinical HIV-1 isolate JR-FL and BG505. The unliganded HIV-1JR-FL and HIV-1BG505 Envs more stably adopted State one as compared to the HIV-1NL4-3 Env.
evidence: This is shown by comparing FRET histograms and free energy calculations in Figure 4B and C.

claim: The energy of State 1 of HIV-1JR-FL and HIV-1BG505 was lower than that of State 2 by 1.05 kBT and 1.16 kBT, respectively, as compared to 0.37 kBT for NL4-3.
source: Specifically, the energy of State 1 of HIV-1JR-FL and HIV-1BG505 was lower than that of State 2 by 1.05 kBT and 1.16 kBT, respectively, as compared to 0.37 kBT for NL4-3 (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is calculated from FRET histogram occupancies shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: Addition of the dodecameric sCD4D1D2-Igαtp stabilized State 3, decreasing the energy to 0.6 kBT and 0.79 kBT lower than that of State 2 of HIV-1JR-FL and HIV-1BG505, respectively.
source: Importantly, as was observed for HIV-1NL4-3 Env, addition of the dodecameric sCD4D1D2-Igαtp stabilized State 3 (Figure 4B and C, right), decreasing the energy to 0.6 kBT and 0.79 kBT lower than that of State 2 of HIV-1JR-FL and HIV-1BG505, respectively. (Figure 4B and C, right).
evidence: This is calculated from FRET histogram occupancies shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: HIV-1JR-FL and HIVBG505 Envs were not as dramatically stabilized in State two by sCD4 binding as was observed for HIV-1NL4-3 Env.
source: Interestingly, HIV-1JR-FL and HIVBG505 Envs were not as dramatically stabilized in State two by sCD4 binding as was observed for HIV-1NL4-3 Env.
evidence: This is shown by comparing FRET histograms in Figure 4B and C with Figure 4A.

claim: Binding of sCD4 and sCD4D1D2-Igαtp to HIV-1JR-FL and HIV-1BG505 Env exhibited similar tendencies in the stabilization of State two as well as State 3.
source: Rather, binding of sCD4 and sCD4D1D2-Igαtp to HIV-1JR-FL and HIV-1BG505 Env exhibited similar tendencies in the stabilization of State two as well as State 3.
evidence: This is shown by comparing FRET histograms in Figure 4B and C.

claim: sCD4D1D2-Igαtp was clearly more efficient in promoting the accumulation of molecules in the State three conformation.
source: sCD4D1D2-Igαtp was clearly more efficient in promoting the accumulation of molecules in the State three conformation.
evidence: This is shown by comparing FRET histograms for sCD4 vs sCD4D1D2-Igαtp.

claim: While there are distinct differences in the ability of sCD4 to activate Env for all three strains, the potent dodecameric sCD4D1D2-Igαtp stabilizes Envs from all three isolates in the open conformation (State 3).
source: Thus, while there are distinct differences in the ability of sCD4 to activate Env for all three strains, the potent dodecameric sCD4D1D2-Igαtp stabilizes Envs from all three isolates in the open conformation (State 3).
evidence: This is shown by comparing FRET histograms across all three strains with sCD4D1D2-Igαtp.

claim: The most populated FRET State one corresponds to the gp120 conformation of the mature pre-triggered Env trimer.
source: Here we used smFRET to identify the nature of the three conformational states sampled by HIV-1 Env (Munro et al., 2014). The most populated FRET State one corresponds to the gp120 conformation of the mature pre-triggered Env trimer.
evidence: This is supported by multiple lines of evidence including antibody binding and population analysis.

claim: The State three stabilization by oligomerized sCD4D1D2-Igαtp, sCD4 and 17b, and the CD4 mimetic small molecule JRC-II-191 indicated that State three corresponds to the gp120 conformation of the open, three-CD4-bound trimer.
source: The State three stabilization by oligomerized sCD4D1D2-Igαtp, sCD4 and 17b, and the CD4 mimetic small molecule JRC-II-191 (Munro et al., 2014), indicated that State three corresponds to the gp120 conformation of the open, three-CD4-bound trimer.
evidence: This is inferred from the consistent stabilization of State 3 by different CD4-mimicking ligands.

claim: The most prevalent default intermediate State two is an asymmetric Env trimer configuration engaging a single CD4 molecule.
source: By using a mixed trimer assay, we identified the most prevalent default intermediate State two to be an asymmetric Env trimer configuration engaging a single CD4 molecule.
evidence: This is supported by mixed trimer experiments.

claim: The individual protomers within the asymmetric trimer adopted different conformations, and State two population originated from the two unbound protomers adjacent to the single CD4-bound protomer.
source: The individual protomers within the asymmetric trimer adopted different conformations, and State two population originated from the two unbound protomers adjacent to the single CD4-bound protomer.
evidence: This is supported by mixed trimer 1 and 2 experiments showing different FRET states for different protomers.

claim: The unliganded trimer resides predominantly in a conformation in which all three protomers are in the pre-triggered State one configuration, which can be represented as the (1,1,1) configuration.
source: The unliganded trimer resides predominantly in a conformation in which all three protomers are in the pre-triggered State one configuration, which can be represented as the (1,1,1) configuration (where each of the three numbers defines the FRET state of each protomer within the trimer).
evidence: This is inferred from FRET histogram showing predominant State 1 for unliganded Env.

claim: Binding of a single CD4 molecule induces conformational changes in the CD4-bound protomer, such that the trimer adopts a (3,2,2) configuration.
source: Binding of a single CD4 molecule then induces conformational changes in the CD4-bound protomer, such that the trimer adopts a (3,2,2) configuration.
evidence: This is inferred from mixed trimer experiments showing State 3 in CD4-bound protomer and State 2 in adjacent protomers.

claim: In the (3,2,2) configuration, the CD4-bound protomer exhibits intermediate-FRET (State 3), while the two neighboring protomers exhibit high-FRET (State 2).
source: In the (3,2,2) configuration, the CD4-bound protomer exhibits intermediate-FRET (State 3), while the two neighboring protomers exhibit high-FRET (State 2).
evidence: This is inferred from mixed trimer experiments.

claim: The near absence of direct transitions between State one to State three suggests that the trimer opening likely occurs through a conformational intermediate with a FRET value similar to State two such as a (2,1,1) or (2,2,2) configuration.
source: The near absence of direct transitions between State one to State three suggests that the trimer opening likely occurs through a conformational intermediate with a FRET value similar to State two such as a (2,1,1) or (2,2,2) configuration.
evidence: This is inferred from the transition density plots showing rare State 1 to State 3 transitions.

claim: The complete activation of HIV-1 Env likely requires either a local clustering of CD4 or coreceptor binding.
source: The complete activation of HIV-1 Env then likely requires either a local clustering of CD4 or coreceptor binding.
evidence: This is inferred from experiments showing State 3 stabilization with multiple CD4 or coreceptor.

claim: Local clustering of CD4 or coreceptor binding would induce the Env trimer to reach more open configurations (either (3,3,2) or (3,3,3)).
source: This would induce of the Env trimer to reach more open configurations (either (3,3,2) or (3,3,3)) (Yang et al., 2006; Salzwedel and Berger, 2009; Ozorowski et al., 2017).
evidence: This is inferred from mixed trimer 3 data and supported by citations.

claim: Coreceptor binding leads to the activation of gp41 and the induction of additional conformational changes necessary for membrane fusion.
source: Coreceptor binding then leads to the activation of gp41 and the induction of additional conformational changes necessary for membrane fusion (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is established knowledge about HIV-1 entry mechanism.

claim: During the spontaneous opening and closing of the HIV-1 Env trimer between States 1 and 3, it is possible that the opening protomer does not fully adopt the three-CD4-bound conformation.
source: During the spontaneous opening and closing of the HIV-1 Env trimer between States 1 and 3, it is possible that the opening protomer does not fully adopt the three-CD4-bound conformation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed dynamics.

claim: The opening protomer may only partially open, just far enough for the trimer apex to be disrupted and the adjacent protomers adopting the State two high-FRET conformation.
source: Rather it may only partially open, just far enough for the trimer apex to be disrupted and the adjacent protomers adopting the State two high-FRET conformation.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of spontaneous opening.

claim: Asymmetric structural intermediates during the activation of viral fusion machines may be more common than previously thought.
source: In this paper, we used smFRET to reveal asymmetric trimer configurations in the opening of the HIV-1 Env trimer. Asymmetric structural intermediates during the activation of viral fusion machines may be more common than previously thought.
evidence: This is speculation based on the current findings and comparison with other viruses.

claim: Single receptor engagement and sequential shedding has been observed for the Murine Leukemia Virus (MLV) Env.
source: Single receptor engagement and sequential shedding has been observed for the Murine Leukemia Virus (MLV) Env (Riedel et al., 2017; Sjöberg et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on MLV.

claim: A recent study on the activation of pre-fusion HIV-1 gp41 to downstream intermediate states suggested that gp41 also opens through asymmetric intermediates.
source: And a recent study on the activation of pre-fusion HIV-1 gp41 to downstream intermediate states suggested that gp41 also opens through asymmetric intermediates (Khasnis et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a study on gp41.

claim: The labeling efficiencies of the Q3 and A1 tags are 40% and 55%, respectively.
source: Under these conditions, the labeling efficiencies of the Q3 and A1 tags are 40% and 55%, respectively (Munro et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work characterizing the labeling system.

claim: The infectivity of D368R mutant was reduced by ~100 fold compared to WT.
source: Their infectivity was reduced by ~100 fold, but the signal to noise ratio in our experiments was orders of magnitude above background permitting a neutralization assay and demonstrating the resistance of D368R to sCD4 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.
